ground.purpose: The shell and the sidebar; the tone of anything that holds other things on the sheet (user turn, run readout, ledger tray, tab tracks). Dark: oklch(0.17 0.006 60).

background.purpose: The floating surface: header, transcript, instrument, /harness pages. Dark: oklch(0.212 0.007 60).

foreground.purpose: Body text. 16.47:1 on the sheet light, 15.25:1 dark. Dark: oklch(0.95 0.006 75).

card.purpose: One step above the sheet: composer, tool card, outline button face. Dark: oklch(0.235 0.008 60).

sidebar-accent.purpose: A selected row on the ground, lifted to the sheet colour (with shadow-sheet). Dark: oklch(0.24 0.008 60).

secondary.purpose: Toggle-on fill. Same value as accent. Dark: oklch(0.27 0.008 60).

accent.purpose: Hover fill on the sheet. Dark: oklch(0.27 0.008 60).

muted.purpose: Same value as ground in light. Dark: oklch(0.27 0.008 60).

muted-foreground.purpose: Metadata. 6.20:1 sheet, 5.46:1 ground, 5.35:1 accent (light). Dark: oklch(0.72 0.013 70).

primary.purpose: Every filled control (Send, New chat). Inverts in dark: oklch(0.93 0.008 75). Never a hue.

primary-foreground.purpose: Text on Warm Ink, 14.70:1 light. Dark: oklch(0.22 0.01 55).

input.purpose: Resting edge of fields, outline buttons and the composer. Dark: oklch(0.95 0.02 70 / 16%).

ring.purpose: Focus indicator: 4.24:1 sheet, 4.30:1 card, 3.74:1 ground (light). Dark: oklch(0.6 0.015 70).

code-surface.purpose: The slab under code and shell output. Dark: oklch(0.18 0.006 60).

scrollbar-thumb.purpose: A control, 3:1 owed: 3.90:1 sheet, 3.44:1 ground. Dark: oklch(0.62 0.01 70).

state-blocked.purpose: A person is being asked to act. Dark: oklch(0.879 0.169 91.605).

state-running.purpose: In flight, or rejoining. Dark: oklch(0.828 0.111 230.318).

destructive.purpose: A solid fill carrying white, for destructive actions only. Dark: oklch(0.704 0.191 22.216).

recording.purpose: The microphone while recording; red by convention, not a failure. Dark: oklch(0.72 0.19 24).

display.purpose: The empty thread's welcome headline only. 24px rising to 28px at md.

figure.purpose: The Activity account sentence, and (in mono) the Where-the-spend-went total. 24px.

statement.purpose: An approval's summary, the run readout's state word, the "This run" heading. 18px.

headline.purpose: PageSection h3, the uppercase wordmark, gate and crash headings. 16px.

prose.purpose: Transcript bodies and the composer textarea, one size so a message does not change size when sent.

title.purpose: Panel and disclosure headers, every button and tab label. 14px semibold.

body.purpose: Rows, controls, instructional copy, an approval's reason and grant sentence. 14px.

label.purpose: Metadata, counts, chips, group labels, speaker labels. 12px is the floor.

value.purpose: JetBrains Mono. Anything the harness emitted: ids, paths, tool names, JSON, token counts.

shadows.name: shadow-sheet
shadows.purpose: Set on a tone: the floating sheet, the current thread tile, active sidebar row, active tab pill, a tool card, a ledger tile.

shadows.name: shadow-lift (--shadow-composer)
shadows.purpose: The primary action floats: the resting composer and the New chat pill.

shadows.name: shadow-lift-focus (--shadow-composer-focus)
shadows.purpose: The focused composer and its slash menu (reached through the variable; the utility has no user).

shadows.name: shadow-approval
shadows.value: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklch, var(--state-blocked) 10%, transparent), 0 4px 8px oklch(0.3 0.03 55 / 8%), 0 20px 44px -10px oklch(0.3 0.03 55 / 22%)
shadows.dark: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklch, var(--state-blocked) 12%, transparent), 0 4px 8px oklch(0 0 0 / 40%), 0 20px 44px -10px oklch(0 0 0 / 60%)
shadows.purpose: A run waiting on a person: the one lift above the focused composer, with an amber halo.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.purpose: Disclosure chevrons, hover colour, a thread row's action fade.

motion.name: surface-transition
motion.purpose: The composer's border and lift on focus, rails and drawers opening, the composer settling after the first message. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Live words only, swept toward the foreground so the text only brightens. Stops, words unchanged, under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: working-pulse
motion.purpose: "Still working" slows rather than stopping, because frozen it reports a live run as hung.

breakpoints.name: instrument-inline
breakpoints.purpose: Above this the run instrument is an inline column; below it a drawer. It yields first because it is reference material.

breakpoints.name: sidebar-inline
breakpoints.purpose: Above this the sidebar is inline and the sheet floats (8px off top, bottom and right, 22px radius, shadow-sheet); below it the sidebar is a drawer and the sheet is edge to edge.

breakpoints.name: harness-nav
breakpoints.purpose: /harness draws its own nav rail only between this and 1024px; below it the index is the list.

breakpoints.name: instrument-default-open
breakpoints.purpose: Where the instrument starts open; a stored choice outranks it.

breakpoints.name: rise
breakpoints.purpose: Where the empty thread's composer rises to meet the greeting.

layoutTokens.name: --header-height
layoutTokens.purpose: Shared by the header and the toast layer's offset.

layoutTokens.name: --z-toast
layoutTokens.purpose: One step above every portalled primitive at z-50.

layoutTokens.name: --radius
layoutTokens.purpose: Root of the radius scale: sm 10, md 12, lg 14, xl 18, 2xl 22.

layoutTokens.name: sheet-inset
layoutTokens.purpose: How far the sheet floats off the ground from 1024px.

layoutTokens.name: sidebar-width
layoutTokens.purpose: The app sidebar on the ground.

layoutTokens.name: instrument-width
layoutTokens.purpose: The run instrument widens on a large display, not the transcript.

layoutTokens.name: transcript-measure
layoutTokens.purpose: The transcript, every /harness page and instrument section, centred on the sheet.

narrative.overview:
This is not a chat app that happens to log tool calls; it is a window onto a running process that happens to accept messages. The mounted folder is the subject, the thread is how you talk to it, and the machinery is on display because supervising it is the job. It is read daily by one operator who ran the harness themselves and holds the gate key, so density, learned affordances, and labels that assume the harness was configured by the reader are all permitted. What is not permitted is a tidier abstraction standing in front of what the harness actually reported.

Since 2026-10-10 the *material* is warm, because this is a tool opened every day. A stone ground carries the shell and the sidebar; a near-white sheet floats on it and holds everything that is read. Soft radii go on what is touched, a humanist grotesk (Onest) carries prose and UI, and a mono (JetBrains Mono) marks what the harness said. The register underneath is unchanged: **instrumented, calm, exact**. Instrumented: real states, real numbers, real event types. Calm: no alarm colours for ordinary states, no motion competing with streaming text, no celebration. Exact: a number is a number. Warmth is a property of the surface, never of the facts. It never swaps a status for a friendlier one, never hides a call, and never adds a colour that does not mean state.

The confirmed anti-references are specific. The **scaffolded AI-chat default**: stock shadcn tokens (the zinc palette this redesign replaced), the system font, flat hierarchy, bordered cards stacked down every panel, an icon on every row, a gradient somewhere. This redesign was made to leave it. **Density without hierarchy**: every panel equally loud, nowhere for the eye to land. **Consumer-chat fiction**: the inverted user bubble, the avatar, statuses softened into reassurance, the harness tucked out of sight. Warmth is now the chosen register, and the fiction stays out. The empty thread's welcome headline and starter cards are kept by choice: they are confined to the empty thread and gone once the first message lands. **Warm-neutral editorial**: cream, serif display, marketing cadence. The ground is stone, never cream, and the face is a sans.
keyCharacteristics: Two neutral levels: a warm stone ground under a near-white floating sheet. Colour means run state and nothing else.
Tone and one confident scale step for separation; hairlines only where tone cannot do it.
One header grammar (icon, title, one at-a-glance value) repeated at every scale.
Monospace for anything the harness emitted; Onest for anything we wrote.
A 12/14/16 ramp, with single steps at 18, 20 and 24 reserved for named roles.
Pills for what you press, 22px corners for what you read or decide on.
Four shadows, each a role: the sheet, the lift, the focused lift, the approval.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Colour is the fastest channel for "healthy / waiting / failed", and spending it on decoration spends the operator's attention. Outside the four-hue ramp, the destructive action colour and the recording indicator, the interface is warm neutral. There is no brand accent; warmth lives in the neutrals' hue, never in a fifth colour.

rules.name: The Stone-Not-Cream Rule
rules.body: Neutral chroma stays under 0.01. Above that the ground reads as paper and the surface drifts into the editorial register it is not.

rules.name: The Two-Client Rule
rules.body: The ramp is authored as `oklch()` in `apps/chat-ui/src/index.css` and frozen as sRGB hex in `packages/design/src/tokens.ts`, because neither a terminal nor `RGBA.fromHex` takes `oklch()`. `pnpm check-state-palette` fails when they disagree. The stylesheet is the authored form; never edit the hex to match a change.

rules.name: The Attention-Blocked Rule
rules.body: `blocked` (amber) means a person is being asked to act. `failed` (red) means something already went wrong and nobody is being asked. The approval deadline chip is the rule in one element: amber while a person can still answer, red the moment the harness has answered for them.

rules.name: The Provenance Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks what the harness said; Onest marks what we said. A model id, a path, a tool name, an event type and a raw status are mono because they are quotations. Our own sentences about them are not.

rules.name: The One-Step Rule
rules.body: Each size above 16px belongs to a role, not to a component. Reaching for `text-lg`, `text-xl` or `text-2xl` means claiming Statement, Page Title or Figure; a second use must be the same kind of thing (a question asked, a page named, the number a page is for).

rules.name: Tabular numerals on anything that counts
rules.body: Token meters, durations, countdowns and queue counts change in place; proportional figures make them jitter.

rules.name: The Yield Rule
rules.body: A rail never narrows the thing it describes; it leaves.

rules.name: The Shrink-Floor Rule
rules.body: Anything below a scrolling region carries `flexShrink: 0`. A transcript longer than the screen will otherwise eat the composer's rows and leave a box you cannot type in, with nothing on screen to say why.

rules.name: Zones move at one speed
rules.body: An inline rail opens and closes by animating its width: `RailPresence` interpolates a grid track between `0fr` and `1fr`, so the transcript beside it reflows over 200ms `ease-out` instead of jumping. The rail's content keeps its own width and is clipped rather than squeezed, and a closing rail is `inert` until it unmounts. The narrow-width drawers slide at the same 200ms `ease-out`. Both are off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.

rules.name: The Four Lifts Rule
rules.body: Sheet means set on a tone; lift means the primary action; focused lift means the primary action in use; approval means a person is being waited on. A new surface takes the lift its role already names. A fifth shadow is a new role and needs a reason that none of the four covers.

rules.name: The Approval-Owns-Attention Rule
rules.body: Nothing on screen out-ranks a waiting approval: its lift, border and radius are the largest on the sheet. A new element that competes with it is wrong.

rules.name: The Nesting Rule
rules.body: A pane takes whichever tonal level its container does not: on the sheet it is `bg-code-surface`, inside a card it is `bg-background`. Both are flat colours, never alphas. `bg-solid-<token>/<n>` (a tint mixed with `--background` rather than with transparent) is the spelling for a tint that must be one flat colour whatever sits behind it.

rules.name: The Soft-Where-Touched Rule
rules.body: The larger a thing is as an object of attention, the larger its corner; a pill is for pressing. An object never takes a pill, and a control never takes a 22px card corner.

rules.name: The Cancelled-Not-Gone Rule
rules.body: A call that changed nothing keeps its card. It is drawn with a dashed `state-failed/40` border and its summary struck through (`decoration-state-failed/60`), so it still reads as something that was tried. Nothing disappears; it cancels.

dos: Do spend colour on run state and nothing else: the four-hue ramp, `destructive` for a destructive action, `recording` for the microphone. Warmth lives in the neutrals.
Do put the shell and the sidebar on the stone ground and everything read on the sheet.
Do give every panel header one at-a-glance value.
Do set monospace for anything the harness emitted and Onest for anything we wrote.
Do set what is read at 16px and what is scanned at 12/14px, and give 18/20/24px only to Statement, Page Title and Figure.
Do separate with tone first: a stone tray under white tiles, a stone note in white space.
Do keep a failed or refused call on screen, dashed and struck through.
Do carry `flexShrink: 0` on anything below a scrolling region.
Do measure contrast in each theme in its natural state, on both neutral levels.
Do state the resting case. A signal that appears only in trouble teaches the operator not to look at it.
donts: Don't add a brand accent colour. "You can act here" is warm ink, never a fifth hue. The mark's cursor is ink at rest and a state's hue only when there is a state.
Don't let the neutrals' chroma rise above 0.01 or move the ground toward cream.
Don't hand-edit a rendered mark. Change `packages/design/src/mark.ts` and run `pnpm sync:brand`.
Don't stack bordered cards down a panel. Objects go on a tray as tiles; readouts are rows.
Don't put an icon on every row. Icons mark kinds, not rows.
Don't draw a user turn as an inverted or side-aligned bubble, or give either speaker an avatar.
Don't introduce a fifth shadow, and don't read the vendored primitives' shadcn defaults as licence for one.
Don't put anything on the sheet that out-ranks a waiting approval.
Don't pill a button whose label may wrap to two lines; use `rounded-xl`.
Don't encode a status in colour alone, and don't use amber and red interchangeably.
Don't edit the frozen hex in `packages/design/src/tokens.ts` to resolve a palette mismatch.
Don't drop below 12px to gain density.
Don't add motion that competes with streaming text, and honour `prefers-reduced-motion`. A "still working" pulse or spinner slows under reduced motion rather than stopping.
